entries.notes: Depends on ConvertSpecialTrainerCardToPokemon, now translated from ROM-extracted local template.
SRAM enable/bank hardware is represented by explicit banked memory; payload/header/checksum semantics are source exact.
Standalone TCG entry reproduces the source WRAM0/HRAM clear ranges.

Common damage arithmetic/order is translated, including changed color/weakness/resistance, double-damage substatus, PlusPower/Defender, reduction substatuses, Invisible Wall/Kabuto Armor and source 16-bit underflow behavior.
Generic phase lookup/dispatch is driven by ROM-verified effect-command lists; untranslated function identities fail closed.

Generic effect families include all 81/81 unique EFFECTCMDTYPE_AI identities, all 45/45 unique EFFECTCMDTYPE_AI_SELECTION identities, and all 5/5 unique EFFECTCMDTYPE_AI_SWITCH_DEFENDING_PKMN identities. Metronome player execution now selects a non-Power defending attack, rejects recursive Metronome, runs copied INITIAL_EFFECT_1/2 through the normal dispatcher, preserves nested copied-attack selection state, and leaves the copied attack loaded for the outer discard/selection/damage/after-damage pipeline. Unknown function identities still fail closed.
State/arithmetic paths translated; cartridge menu/animation presentation remains adapter-owned.
State/arithmetic paths translated; cartridge menu/animation presentation remains adapter-owned.
State behavior translated, including play-area Pokemon Power damage prevention/reduction; presentation text/animation remains outside this layer.
State/color accounting used by Rain Dance and Charizard Energy Burn; presentation is not part of these routines.
State path includes ordinary once-per-turn attachment and the Blastoise Rain Dance Water-to-Water exception; menu/link presentation remains adapter-owned.
Includes the source card-ID dispatcher and cartridge quirks such as Earthquake pointer/prize-side bugs; unknown flagged cards fail closed.
Native AI retreat-cost calculation applies each benched Dodrio Retreat Aid and preserves Muk suppression/clamping.
Exact 0/25/50% source gate by progress state and opponent deck class; used by common Trainer processing and Energy Trans.
Source decision rules and documented cartridge quirks are native; execution reuses the translated generic Trainer/effect-command path.

Source decision priorities are native, including Rain Dance retrieval gating, Super Energy Removal target/energy ordering, Gust of Wind bench selection, and deck-specific Poke Ball branches. Trainer execution reuses the translated generic effect path.

Common active Pokemon Power AI is native, including source random cadence, once-per-turn/status gating, target selection, compacted-play-area Cowardice rescans, Damage Swap fallback-target quirk, and Curse KO targeting.
State semantics for the seven common manual Pokemon Power families are native; UI/presentation loops remain host-owned.
All source card-ID branches are native: Mew Lv23 Devolution Beam, both Mewtwo Lv60 Energy Absorption variants, Exeggutor Teleport, and Electrode Lv35 Energy Spike.
Source-ordered common scoring now includes KO/damage/status/discard/heal terms, defending-KO interaction, full LOW/HIGH_RECOIL policy, and SPECIAL_AI_HANDLING dispatch.

Active and Bench forward/reverse estimators are slot-aware, preserve switch-sensitive temporary-state clearing, attached PlusPower/Defender locations, active-only reduction, source poison windows, and exact-KO behavior.

Outer attack orchestration now preserves PlusPower override, second-attack ties, Barrier early exit, preview-with-score-restore behavior, phase-14 Trainer ordering, retreat-pressure updates, selection preparation and attack-attempt semantics.

Normal Energy placement and all source preview modes are native: evolution anticipation, Venusaur/Barrier/poison/KO/low-HP scoring, generated per-deck caps/bonuses, Legendary Articuno priorities, repeated-Bench scoring, attached-energy-boost/discard branches, special DCE anticipation, boss DCE avoidance, Energy Spike skip-evolution preview, and the Energy Trans skip-evolution/skip-Arena score-backup preview.

The general (non-Imakuni-deck) branch reads wAIBarrierFlagCounter's AI_MEWTWO_MILL bit, which is only ever written by the still-pending InitAITurnVars Mewtwo-mill identification branch (see that entry in behavior_pending.json); until that lands this branch is correctly always false, matching real hardware with the flag never raised. AIPlay_Gambler's RNG-forcing byte-poke (wRNG1/wRNG2/wRNGCounter set to $50 for every deck but Imakuni?'s own) is reproduced mechanically; running it through the real RNG module shows it actually yields tails, not the heads the source's own comment claims.

Rewritten from a fixed per-phase Trainer-name priority list into a faithful hand-snapshot, hand-order scan matching CreateHandCardList + the AITrainerCardLogic table lookup: cards are considered in hand order (not this file's authoring order in AI_TRAINER_PHASES, whose per-phase membership was already byte-verified against the real table and is unchanged), CheckCantUseTrainerDueToEffect and the card's own EFFECTCMDTYPE_INITIAL_EFFECT_1 gate now run before AIChooseRandomlyNotToDoAction and the card-specific AIDecide_* routine, a successful play that leaves AI_FLAG_MODIFIED_HAND set in wPreviousAIFlags forces a fresh snapshot and restarts the scan from the top (clearing the flag) rather than the prior special-cased Bill-only relist hack, and SWITCH never matches once AI_FLAG_USED_SWITCH is already set. Verified against a real LuaJIT execution fixture (25 checks) covering hand-order iteration, both gates' ordering, the relist restart and flag-clear, the no-relist continuation path, and the SWITCH skip.

The reshuffle-until-satisfied threshold loop (>=2 Basic/Energy in the new 7-card hand, >=4/>=4 counting the following 6) and the final draw are native. The source's own .CheckIfIDIsInList prize-avoidance check has a real bug (`cp a` where `or a` was clearly intended) that makes it unconditionally report "not found" regardless of wAICardListAvoidPrize's contents; that dead branch is documented rather than reproduced as a functioning filter.

Arena placement from wAICardListArenaPriority (fail closed to "no Play Area set up" if absent or no hand match) followed by Bench placement from wAICardListBenchPriority until either that list is exhausted or the Play Area reaches 3 Pokemon, both reading the same generated per-deck list data already used elsewhere via _deckAIList.

Full target-priority cascade: KO-then-usability starting-point gate, first-match enough-to-attack scan, Bench-only highest-damage fallback. A third source fallback (re-checking the Player's Active specifically) is a dead branch (documented, not reimplemented) -- see AI:_decideEnergyRemoval's own comment.

General path plus both deck-specific handlers: LegendaryArticuno (ArticunoLv37-on-Bench Snorlax/no-energy gate, or Arena Articuno/Chansey KO-danger branch sharing the general path's own switch-target tail) and LegendaryRonald (Articuno/Zapdos/Moltres-on-Bench, no Arena branch).

All four decks that can ever play this card: RockCrusher (3-hand-card Professor Oak case, and the Geodude/Graveler-Golem-Dugtrio evolution chain), WondersOfScience (Oak, then Grimer, then Muk), FireCharge (Chansey/Tauros/JigglypuffLv12 priority), and Anger (reuses AIDecide_Pokeball's own LookForCardIDInDeck_GivenCardIDInHand[AndPlayArea] primitives). The real shuffle-then-first-match discard-pair search (RemoveFromListDifferentCardOfGivenType) runs against the actual RNG.

All ten decks: LegendaryMoltres/StrangePower (shared LookForCardIDToTradeWithDifferentHandCard), LegendaryArticuno (bespoke Seel/Dewgong search), LegendaryDragonite (Energy/Pokemon-count gate then evolution chain), LegendaryRonald (Eeveelutions + Dratini chain, single-copy trade-away), BlisteringPokemon/PowerGenerator/FlowerGarden/Flamethrower (evolution chain + FindDuplicatePokemonCards, including its documented 'last duplicate pair wins' quirk), SoundOfTheWaves (evolution chain + spare-copy trade-away). PowerGenerator's own missing `jr .no_carry` (register-garbage fallthrough on total chain failure) is documented, not reimplemented -- fails closed instead.
